newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Communist chief, predecessor investigated.
newsitem.headline: French Communist chief, predecessor investigated.

text.p: Robert Hue, head of the French Communist Party, and his predecessor Georges Marchais have been formally placed under investigation for alleged influence peddling, justice sources said on Monday.
France has been rocked by a string of political funding scandals in recent years, affecting all mainstream parties. But none has reached so high into a party's leadership.
The sources said the probe led by Paris magistrate Laurence Vichnievsky was part of an investigation into illicit funding of the PCF.
The ebullient Hue and the hardliner Marchais were reportedly placed under investigation last week, a step which could lead to a trial but does not imply guilt.
In an unconfirmed report, France-2 television said that party treasurer Pierre Sotura was also placed under investigation for alleged influence peddling.

The judge had searched Communist Party headquarters in June in a probe over the disappearance of nearly 13 million francs (2.5 million) in suspicious billing paid by the French utilities giant Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) in 1992-1994 when some 70 primarily leftist towns were preparing to award water contracts.
In a statement, the party branded last week's judicial move "a serious political event, an attack against the Communist Party".

It said that party finances were transparent and that its accounts were public, denying that it had been paid even a centime (cent) by the Gifco group, parent company of the private consulting firm Sicopar which is suspected of acting as a middle-man in the case.

In May, four former Sicopar managers were placed under investigation in connexion with the case on suspicion of acting as intermediaries. The CGE's deputy general manager, Jean-Dominique Deschamps, has also been placed under investigation in the case.
Sotura had at the time denied any wrongdoing. "Its finances are healthy and totally transparent," he said.

Communist party funding and a CGE water contract is at the heart of another probe led by magistrate Renaud Van Ruymbecke in Rennes in western France. In that case, another consulting firm is suspected of handling an illicit payment of 1.8 million francs ($360,000) in 1988.

Overlord of France's biggest opposition group when he took over as secretary-general in 1972, Marchais saw the PCF's share of the vote fall from 25 to just seven per cent as the Soviet communism that inspired him was discredited and then swept away.
His fast-talking successor Hue, who took over two years ago, is striving to change the party's image.

In a landmark policy shift at the start of last year's presidential election campaign, Hue repudiated Marchais' judgement that communist rule in the former Soviet Union and eastern Europe was "globally positive".
"Regimes in the east were the perversion of communism...We were wrong not to break sooner with that model," Hue said.
